title: C-Suite & Boardroom Politics
completion_message: ¡Excelente! La política de la sala de juntas (Boardroom Politics) es implacable. Conceptos como 'Glass ceiling', 'Golden parachute' o 'Stakeholder' te dan la profundidad necesaria para entender y participar en el juego de tronos del mundo corporativo.

stages.title: Política en la Sala de Juntas (C2)

parts.visual:
1. The C-Suite (La alta dirección): 
- Refiere a los altos ejecutivos cuyos títulos empiezan con 'C' (Chief): CEO, CFO, COO, CTO. 
Ej: The decision must be approved by the C-Suite. 

2. Board of Directors / The Board (Junta Directiva): 
- Grupo elegido por los accionistas (shareholders) para supervisar la empresa. 

3. Stakeholder vs Shareholder: 
- Shareholder: Accionista (dueño de acciones). 
- Stakeholder: Parte interesada (cualquiera afectado por la empresa: empleados, clientes, comunidad). 
Ej: We must consider the impact on all stakeholders, not just the shareholders.
parts.audio: Welcome to Boardroom Politics. Number 1: The C-Suite. This refers to the top senior executives whose titles start with 'Chief', like CEO, CFO, COO, and CTO. Number 2: The Board of Directors, or simply 'The Board'. This is the group elected by shareholders to oversee the company. Number 3: Stakeholder versus Shareholder. A 'shareholder' owns shares of the company. A 'stakeholder' is anyone affected by the company, including employees, customers, and the community. For example: We must consider the impact on all stakeholders, not just the shareholders.

parts.visual:
Términos Políticos Corporativos: 

4. Golden parachute (Paracaídas de oro): 
- Una gran compensación financiera garantizada a un ejecutivo si es despedido o la empresa es vendida. 
Ej: The CEO left with a $20 million golden parachute. 

5. Glass ceiling (Techo de cristal): 
- Una barrera invisible que impide a ciertos grupos (frecuentemente mujeres o minorías) ascender a los puestos más altos. 
Ej: She finally broke the glass ceiling and became the first female CEO. 

6. Nepotism / Cronyism (Nepotismo / Amiguismo): 
- Contratar o ascender a familiares (nepotism) o amigos (cronyism) sin importar el mérito.
parts.audio: Corporate Political Terms. Number 4: Golden parachute. This is a massive financial compensation guaranteed to an executive if they are fired or the company is sold. For example: The CEO left with a twenty million dollar golden parachute. Number 5: Glass ceiling. An invisible barrier that prevents certain demographics, often women or minorities, from rising to the highest levels. For example: She finally broke the glass ceiling and became the first female CEO. Number 6: Nepotism and Cronyism. 'Nepotism' is favoring relatives, while 'Cronyism' is favoring friends, regardless of their actual merit.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término correcto sobre política corporativa.

questions.question: The group of top senior executives (CEO, CFO, CTO) is collectively known as the ____-Suite.
A person who owns shares in a company is a ____.
Anyone who has an interest in or is affected by the company (employees, customers, local community) is a ____.
The CEO was fired, but he received a massive ____ parachute as part of his severance package.
Many women in the corporate world still struggle to break through the ____ ceiling.
The manager was accused of ____ because he hired his unqualified nephew for the job.
Promoting his unqualified college friend over experienced employees is a clear case of ____. (Amiguismo).
The group elected by shareholders to oversee the company is the ____ of Directors.
A secret agreement or cooperation between competitors to fix prices or cheat others is called ____. (Colusión).
An attempt by an outside company to take over a target company against the wishes of its management is a ____ takeover.
questions.explanation: Hostile takeover = OPA hostil / toma de control hostil.

questions.question: When an executive uses confidential company information to buy or sell stock illegally, it's called ____ trading.
questions.explanation: Insider trading = uso de información privilegiada.

questions.question: An employee who publicly exposes illegal or unethical practices within their own company is a ____. (Denunciante).
A strategy used by a target company to prevent a hostile takeover by making its stock less attractive is a ____ pill. (Píldora envenenada).
questions.explanation: Poison pill = píldora envenenada (estrategia anti-OPA hostil).

questions.question: The Chief ____ Officer (CFO) is responsible for managing the financial risks of the corporation.
The Chief ____ Officer (COO) oversees the daily operations of the company.
A company that holds a controlling interest in other companies (subsidiaries) is called a ____ company. (Empresa matriz/holding).
A situation in which a person is in a position to derive personal benefit from actions or decisions made in their official capacity is a ____ of interest.
questions.explanation: Conflict of interest = conflicto de intereses.

questions.question: When the board forces the CEO to resign but disguises it as a voluntary 'retirement', he was effectively ____ out. (Expulsado/Empujado).
When a company separates part of its business into a completely new, independent company, it's called a ____.
questions.explanation: Spin-off = escisión / creación de una nueva empresa a partir de otra.

questions.question: An individual who is appointed to the board but is not an employee of the company is an ____ director. (Director independiente).
The ____-Suite. (Alta dirección con C)
The ____ of Directors. (Junta Directiva con B)
A ____holder owns stock. (Accionista con S)
A ____holder is affected by the company. (Parte interesada con S)
A ____ parachute. (Indemnización millonaria con G)
The ____ ceiling. (Techo invisible con G)
Hiring family is ____. (Nepotismo con N)
Hiring friends is ____. (Amiguismo con C)
A hostile ____. (Toma de control hostil con T)
A corporate ____. (Denunciante con W)
